content:
We got fragments list, many with negative charges (anion fragments). This suggests the sample may be a carboxylate or something. Fragments like O=[C-]O (carbonate?), C[CH-]C(=O)O (maybe acetate?), C[CH-]C (propyl anion). The presence of C[CH-][CH-]O suggests glycolate? Also CC(C)=C(C)[C-]=O looks like a t-butyl carboxylate anion? Many fragments with C- (carbanion). Could be a neutral molecule that fragments to anions.

Maybe the sample is a neutral organic acid that deprotonates to give these anions. For example, 2-methylpropanoic acid (isobutyric acid) would give fragments like C[CH-]C(=O)O (propionate). But also fragments with double bonds.

Look at fragment "O=[C-]O" is carbonate anion (CO2-). Could be from carboxylic acid.

Fragment "C[CH-][C-]=O" is maybe acetoacetate? Not sure.

Maybe the sample is a simple carboxylate like acetate (CH3COO-). Fragments: C[CH-]C(=O)O (that's CH3-CH-COO-? Actually C[CH-]C(=O)O would be CH3-CH-COO- (propionate). Not acetate.

Fragment "CC(C)=C(C)[C-]=O" is maybe pivalate anion? Pivalic acid (tert-butyl carboxylate) would be (CH3)3C-COO-; fragment could be C[CH-]C(=O)O? Not.

Let's consider the neutral molecule could be a dicarboxylic acid? Fragments include O=[C-]O (CO2-). Also C[CH-][CH-]O (maybe glycolate). Could be malonic acid? Fragments: CH2-COO- etc.

But many fragments have double bonds: CC(C)=C(C)[C-]=O suggests a conjugated system like isobutene carboxylate? That's 3-methyl-2-butenoate? Actually CC(C)=C(C)C(=O)O is 3-methyl-2-butenoic acid (tiglic acid). Its anion would be CC(C)=C(C)[C-]=O. That fragment appears.

Also CC(C)=C(C)[CH-]O appears (maybe hydroxy version). So maybe the molecule is 3-methyl-2-butenoic acid (tiglic acid) or its isomer (angelic acid). Both have formula C5H8O2? Actually tiglic acid C5H8O2 (CH3-CH=C(CH3)-COOH). That could fragment to those.

But also fragments like CC(C)=[C-][CH-]O (maybe unsaturated acid). The presence of many fragments suggests a C5 acid.

Let's try to get formula via get_formula_from_smiles for candidate "CC(C)=C(C)C(=O)O" (tiglic acid).
